extracted_details.description_text: The supplied INF identifies Surface Integration Driver version 120.8.4.0, dated 2026-05-06, for the System class and ACPI\MSHW0530 on 64-bit Windows beginning at build 19041. INFDescriptionData was semantically analyzed: the package installs a demand-start kernel service, three named Surface power-policy packages, and a 14-point display backlight power curve under Windows energy estimation. It also contains settings for KIP support, battery estimate visibility, long-press screen refresh, and BitLocker request limits, but the INF's shown install sections do not reference the section containing those settings, so their application cannot be confirmed. The supplied Intel portals concern Intel Management Engine/chipset software and do not identify this Surface package. The Microsoft Update Catalog searches for version 120.8.4.0 and the package name did not expose a verifiable matching Surface entry or release notes; no previous, latest, or family-version release notes were verified or used.
key_components: SurfaceIntegrationDriver.sys, installed as a demand-start kernel driver
14-point Windows display backlight power curve, with brightness points from 0% to 100%

Separate INF registry section defining PlatformKipSupported, battery-discharge estimate, power-button screen-refresh, and BitLocker request-limit settings; the supplied install-section references do not show that section being applied
key_functionalities: Installs the Surface Integration Driver system service for the INF-declared ACPI\MSHW0530 device.
Copies default and Windows-version-specific Surface power-policy provisioning packages and associates their paths with device properties.
Registers a 14-point brightness-to-backlight-power curve for Windows display energy estimation.
Defines PlatformKipSupported=1, with an INF comment stating that it enables KIP power-saving features; the setting's installation is not confirmed by the shown AddReg references.
Defines settings to hide the estimated remaining battery discharge time and enable screen refresh after a long power-button press; their installation is not confirmed by the shown AddReg references.

Defines BitLocker encrypt, decrypt, and per-I/O crypto request limits of 0x40; the INF comment says the encryption request limit is intended to improve SSD performance under BitLocker, but application of these settings is not confirmed.
extracted_details.major_components_functionalities_descrip: This enrichment uses the exact supplied version 120.8.4.0 and its INF date of 2026-05-06; no exact, previous, latest, or family-version release notes were verified. INFDescriptionData was semantically analyzed and identifies a 64-bit Windows System-class driver for ACPI\MSHW0530, installed as a demand-start kernel service. The package copies default and Windows 10/Windows 11 power-policy provisioning packages and registers a 14-point display backlight curve for energy estimation. Other INF sections define KIP, battery-estimate, screen-refresh, and BitLocker request settings, but the displayed install-section references do not link to that section, so they are not claimed as applied behavior. No official version-specific fixes or changes can be stated from the available sources.
impact_details: Directly affects installation of the Surface Integration kernel service and default/OS-specific power-policy package files for eligible ACPI\MSHW0530 devices.
May affect Windows display energy estimates through the registered brightness-to-backlight-power curve.
The INF defines KIP power-saving support, but the provided install-section links do not establish that this setting is applied.
The INF defines battery discharge estimate and long-press screen-refresh settings, but the provided install-section links do not establish that these settings are applied.
The INF defines BitLocker request limits and comments on intended SSD performance under BitLocker, but the provided install-section links do not establish that the settings are applied.
No supported Surface SKU names or version-specific fixes are provided by the INF or verified release information.

rejected_categories.reason: The SID and KIP tags occur on accessory sub-categories in Categories.json, but their descriptions concern pen charging, haptics, keyboards, touchpads, wireless charging, or accessory state transitions. The INF does not identify or configure those accessory functions, so the tag matches alone do not justify selecting them.

These firmware-oriented sub-categories do not have a matching SID or KIP driverTag for the behavior shown here, and the package installs a System-class kernel driver and policy packages rather than a firmware payload. firmware_flag is false, so firmware-only test scopes are excluded.

Their test scopes are conceptually near the INF's power and battery settings, but the retrieved Categories.json entries use tags such as EC, SAM, and DPTF rather than an exact SID or KIP match. The battery-related registry section is also not linked by the shown install sections, so these sub-categories are not selected.
The retrieved WU_DLC verification entries have no applicable exact SID or KIP driverTag, and the INF does not establish Windows Update delivery or update-servicing behavior for this package.
